Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City Telephone Number 925.11.48 • 925.88.88 • 925.03.32 wv.w.dilg.gov.ph LEGAL SERVICE BAYAN-G MAUNuD DILG Legal Opinion No. 21, S. 2013 05 JUN 2013 CHRIS F. BECH <chris@tablasparadise.com> De r Mr. Bech: This has reference to your letter sent to us thru email dated 19 February 2013 seeking cla 'fication on the extent of the powers of a Mayor. Per your representation, during the time that Mayor Laila Arboleda of Looc, Romblon wa suspended for graft and corruption Dr. Ernesto P. Panes, the acting Mayor, issued a diving permit to Tablas Fun Resort, Inc. (a copy of the permit was attached to your letter). Ho ever, Mayor Arboleda claimed that documents signed by the Acting Mayor are null and voi . Hence, you inquired as to whether "the laws in this country really work that way?" Secondly, you inquired, and we quote "Can a Mayor really decide to prohibit people she Obviously does not like — from utilize (sic) the ocean — which, all over the world, is free for any seaman and boatman to use?" The question stemmed from Mayor Arboleda's decision to prohibit you from utilizing any portion of the Looc Bay for your boating and wawr sport activities. For lack of necessary information and factual background to engender an in depth ana ysis of your queries, we shall confine our answer to the situations and questions presented with some assumptions injected thereto. As to the first query, Mayor Arboleda cannot just set aside the orders/issuances of Dr. Ernesto P. Panes considering that the latter's assumption to the office of mayor of Looc as Acting Mayor was by virtue of succession as provided for by law. Moreover, being the offi ial duly authorized to exercise the functions of the Mayor at that particular time, Dr. Pa es' orders and issuances are presumed valid unless otherwise invalidated by proper aut ority. As to your second query, it is our view that Mayor Arboleda cannot prohibit any peréon from engaging in certain water sport activities in Looc Bay unless there is a duly en eted ordinance prohibiting or at the very least regulating such activity/activities. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. It's more fun in the Phi: Very truly yours, J SUSB. OQ IV Director 111 (4
